The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package and its sources. It does not contain executable code. Both sources are hosted on official, expected domains (github.com and codeload.github.com), which aligns with standard packaging practices.

Checksums are provided for both sources using `b2sums`, with the first source (the cmake repo) marked as `SKIP`. This is acceptable because the source is a Git snapshot tied to a specific commit, and SKIP is commonly used in VCS-based packages when reproducibility via commit hash is sufficient. The second source has a valid b2sum, ensuring integrity. No network operations, file modifications, or execution logic are present in this file — it is purely declarative.

All dependencies listed are standard build-time requirements (cmake, lcms2, libjpeg-turbo, etc.) appropriate for a C/C++ library configuration package. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected downloads, or malicious payloads. The package appears to be a legitimate helper package providing CMake configuration files for LibRaw.
</details>

There are no signs of malicious behavior such as unauthorized network access, obfuscated code, or unexpected file operations.
